# KS-998 — Wednesday's task for Ornith, ITEM 1 ONLY, BASH_PATCH (written 09:58 on 2026-09-16 from the files at develop M55 `48e65c435`: `systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh` lines 100–194 read; `systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate.test.sh` lines 60–140 and 165–171 read) — **KAM RULED 2026-09-16 09:53 (card `secuura-ks998-format-gate-fails-open-on-missing-deps`, option a): "Hard fail ONLY when a tracked file under that package is in the push (the ticket's middle option): a fresh clone pushing unrelated work stays quiet; a push that touches a gated package must have its deps installed."**

## What is wrong (one paragraph)
`check-package-format.sh` (the KS-989 formatting gate the pre-push hook runs) prints `SKIP (advisory)` and counts a skip — exit 0 — when a gated package's `node_modules/.bin/prettier` is missing (`:144-148`). In push mode (`MODE` not `all`, `:115-123`) a package is SELECTED only because a changed path in the push lies under it — so a skip there means **a push that touches the package is waved through unchecked**: the path by which instance 6's red could still reach develop. In `--all` mode (the preflight's whole-tree check) a missing-deps package is a genuine environment condition and the advisory skip is right (KS-991's cost: `DEPS MISSING` read as a red five times in one day). **This task: in push mode a selected package with missing deps is a FAILURE (counted in `failed`, a REFUSED line naming the remedy); in `--all` mode the skip stays. The existing suite's CASE 6 (which pinned the skip in push mode) is flipped to pin the refusal, and CASE 9 (`--all` still skips) stays as the control.** Items 2–4 of the ticket are NOT this task.

## The exact change — ONE REPLACEMENT HUNK in `systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh`: lines 142–148 become the block below
Every line from :142 (`    # Deps absent is an environment condition (see the npm/node note above), and`) through :148 (`    fi`) is a `-` line — copy all 7 from the file byte-for-byte — and the `+` side is EXACTLY this block (14 lines, four-space base indent like its neighbours):
```
-    # Deps absent is an environment condition (see the npm/node note above), and
-    # it is the normal state of a fresh clone. Loud, named, and NOT a failure.
-    if [ ! -x "$dir/node_modules/.bin/prettier" ]; then
-        echo "[format-gate] SKIP (advisory) — systemTest/$p deps not installed (npm ci in systemTest/$p)."
-        skipped=$((skipped + 1))
-        continue
-    fi
+    # Deps absent is an environment condition (see the npm/node note above), and
+    # it is the normal state of a fresh clone — advisory in --all mode. In PUSH mode
+    # this package was selected because the push TOUCHES it (KS-998 item 1, Kam
+    # 2026-09-16): missing deps cannot be advisory there, or the red is pushed unseen.
+    if [ ! -x "$dir/node_modules/.bin/prettier" ]; then
+        if [ "$MODE" != "all" ]; then
+            echo "[format-gate] REFUSED — systemTest/$p deps not installed and this push touches it (npm ci in systemTest/$p, then push again)." >&2
+            failed=$((failed + 1))
+            continue
+        fi
+        echo "[format-gate] SKIP (advisory) — systemTest/$p deps not installed (npm ci in systemTest/$p)."
+        skipped=$((skipped + 1))
+        continue
+    fi
```
(That is 14 lines: four comment lines, the outer `if`, the inner `if … fi` of five lines, the three original skip lines, the closing `fi`.) Context: line 141 is blank and line 140 is `    dir="$REPO_ROOT/systemTest/$p"`; line 149 is blank and line 150 is `    out="$(cd "$dir" && npm run --silent format:check 2>&1)"`. The trailer at `:193-194` (`echo "[format-gate] ${checked} package(s) checked, ${skipped} skipped, ${failed} failed"` / `[ "$failed" -eq 0 ]`) is untouched — `failed` already drives the exit code. Touch nothing else.

## The test — MODIFY THE EXISTING FILE `systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate.test.sh` (its FULL content is in files[...]; your test section is `--- a/…` / `+++ b/…` with context lines copied byte-for-byte; do NOT create a new file, do NOT use `--- /dev/null`)
T1 — REPLACE lines 131–138 (CASE 6: the two comment lines, the `out=`/`rc=` line and its four `check` lines) with the block below (context: line 130 is blank and line 139 is blank; line 140 is `# --- CASE 7: THE COUNTER MUST SURVIVE THE LOOP --------------------------------`):
```
-# --- CASE 6: deps missing is an ENVIRONMENT condition, not a failure ----------
-# KS-991: an environment condition presented as a gate failure cost a diagnosis
-# five times in one day. It must skip, loudly, naming the remedy — and exit 0.
-out="$(run_gate 'systemTest/nodeps/src/a.ts')"; rc=$?
-check "deps missing -> exit 0"                "0" "$rc"
-check "deps missing -> SKIP (advisory)"       "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'SKIP (advisory) — systemTest/nodeps deps not installed')"
-check "deps missing -> names the remedy"      "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'npm ci in systemTest/nodeps')"
-check "deps missing -> counted as skipped"    "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '0 package(s) checked, 1 skipped, 0 failed')"
+# --- CASE 6: deps missing on a package THIS PUSH TOUCHES is a REFUSAL ----------
+# KS-998 item 1 (Kam 2026-09-16): in push mode the package was selected because
+# the push touches it, so missing deps cannot be advisory — the red would be
+# pushed unseen. (--all mode keeps the KS-991 advisory skip: CASE 9 pins it.)
+out="$(run_gate 'systemTest/nodeps/src/a.ts')"; rc=$?
+check "deps missing in push mode -> exit 1"            "1" "$rc"
+check "deps missing in push mode -> REFUSED line"      "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'REFUSED — systemTest/nodeps deps not installed and this push touches it')"
+check "deps missing in push mode -> names the remedy"  "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'npm ci in systemTest/nodeps')"
+check "deps missing in push mode -> counted as failed" "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '0 package(s) checked, 0 skipped, 1 failed')"
```
Nothing else in the test changes. CASE 9 (`:165-171`, `--all` → `4 package(s) checked, 1 skipped, 3 failed`) is the CONTROL that the advisory skip survives in `--all` mode — green on both trees. Why the new CASE 6 is red at the untouched tip: the tip prints `SKIP (advisory)`, exits 0 and counts `1 skipped, 0 failed` — all four new checks fail by value; after the hunk all four pass. The `check` helper (`:40-46`) prints `ok`/`FAIL` lines and the suite's trailer counts them — unchanged.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# The systemTest/* formatting gate (KS-989)
# =============================================================================
# THE DEFECT THIS EXISTS FOR: nothing between a developer's keyboard and
# `develop` ran the per-package format gates for `systemTest/*`. So a docs-only
# or test-only edit under `systemTest/` could turn `npm run format:check` red in
# a package, the author who made it never saw a failure, and the next unrelated
# author to touch that package inherited the red — usually days later, with no
# link back to the commit that caused it.
#
# Three places could have caught it and none of them looked:
#   * `.githooks/pre-push` scopes itself to `^Blockchain/Dev/` — DELIBERATELY,
#     and its own header says so ("skips instantly for vault-only / docs-only /
#     systemTest-only pushes"). The design priced a systemTest-only push as
#     costless. It is not.
#   * `preflight.sh` is invoked BY that hook, so it never ran for these pushes.
#   * GitHub Actions is retired (Kam, 2026-08-27), so there was no backstop.
#
# SIX instances in nine days, three of them found and fixed by someone other
# than the author who caused them (KS-702/#754, KS-706/#755, KS-711/#758,
# KS-707, instance 5 on the trunk at 400517aaf, instance 6 on the trunk at
# 986c592d5). Instance 6 is the one that earned this script: it entered on
# `42e778203` and rode to develop in merge `512480ef1` (#892) — a merge whose
# whole PR lived under `systemTest/`, so the hook skipped it exactly as designed
# and a red sat on the trunk for three hours with nothing looking at it.
#
# --- WHY `format:check` AND NOT `quality` (KS-990) ---------------------------
# `npm run quality` CANNOT PASS in `systemTest/performance` or `systemTest/akto`
# today, for pre-existing reasons unrelated to formatting (a TS2540 read-only
# assignment; two unused knip exports). Wiring `quality` here would produce a
# gate that can never pass — and a gate that can never pass gets bypassed, which
# is the behaviour this ticket exists to stop. It would manufacture it.
# `format:check` is the leg that fires in every instance above, it is green in
# every package as of this commit, and it costs 0–2s per package.
# When KS-990 is closed, widening this to `quality` is a one-word change here.
#
# --- USAGE -------------------------------------------------------------------
#     printf '%s\n' "$paths" | bash systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh
#     bash systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh --all
#     bash systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh --list
#
# Paths on stdin are repo-relative (what `git diff --name-only` emits). Only the
# packages those paths land in are checked. `--all` checks every package and is
# what the caller uses when it cannot compute a reliable changed set — see the
# KS-854/KS-882 note in the hook: an uncomputable base is not a clean tree.
#
# --- PACKAGES ARE DISCOVERED, NOT LISTED -------------------------------------
# Any `systemTest/*/package.json` carrying a `format:check` script is in scope.
# A hardcoded list is a second implementation that something has to keep in
# agreement with reality, and nothing would — the same reasoning that makes
# `run-shell-suites.sh` a glob rather than three pasted copies. Add a package
# with a `format:check` script and it is gated automatically.
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

MODE="stdin"
case "${1:-}" in
    --all)   MODE="all" ;;
    --list)  MODE="list" ;;
    "")      MODE="stdin" ;;
    *) echo "usage: check-package-format.sh [--all|--list]  (default: repo-relative paths on stdin)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

# --- the toolchain, or an honest skip ----------------------------------------
# npm/node missing is an ENVIRONMENT condition, not a finding. KS-991 exists
# because an environment condition was presented as a gate failure and cost a
# diagnosis five times in one day. Say which it is.
if ! command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[format-gate] SKIP (advisory) — node/npm not on PATH; cannot check systemTest formatting."
    exit 0
fi

# --- discover the packages ----------------------------------------------------
# bash 3.2 (what macOS ships, and what the pre-push hook runs) has no
# associative arrays and no mapfile. Plain arrays and a newline-delimited string
# only.
packages=()
for pj in "$REPO_ROOT"/systemTest/*/package.json; do
    [ -e "$pj" ] || continue          # an empty glob expands to itself
    dir="$(dirname "$pj")"
    node -e '
        const s = (require(process.argv[1]).scripts) || {};
        process.exit(s["format:check"] ? 0 : 1);
    ' "$pj" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue
    packages+=("$(basename "$dir")")
done

# `"${arr[@]}"` on an EMPTY array under `set -u` raises "unbound variable" on
# bash 3.2 — and inside a command substitution that error goes to stderr,
# nothing reads it, and the assignment silently yields "". Same trap
# run-shell-suites.sh carries at QA R2-2. Use the +alternate form throughout.
if [ "${#packages[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "[format-gate] SKIP (advisory) — no systemTest package declares a format:check script."
    exit 0
fi

if [ "$MODE" = "list" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "${packages[@]+"${packages[@]}"}"
    exit 0
fi

# --- select the packages this run covers --------------------------------------
changed_paths=""
selected=""
if [ "$MODE" = "all" ]; then
    for p in "${packages[@]+"${packages[@]}"}"; do
        selected="${selected}${p}
"
    done
else
    changed_paths="$(cat)"
    for p in "${packages[@]+"${packages[@]}"}"; do
        if printf '%s\n' "$changed_paths" | grep -q "^systemTest/${p}/"; then
            selected="${selected}${p}
"
        fi
    done
fi

selected="$(printf '%s' "$selected" | grep -v '^$' || true)"
if [ -z "$selected" ]; then
    exit 0                            # nothing under a gated package — say nothing, cost nothing
fi

# --- run it -------------------------------------------------------------------
failed=0
skipped=0
checked=0

# Read the selection line by line rather than relying on word splitting: this
# file is bash, but the same loop pasted into a zsh shell would not split at all
# and would run zero packages while reporting a clean pass.
while IFS= read -r p; do
    [ -n "$p" ] || continue
    dir="$REPO_ROOT/systemTest/$p"

    # Deps absent is an environment condition (see the npm/node note above), and
    # it is the normal state of a fresh clone. Loud, named, and NOT a failure.
    if [ ! -x "$dir/node_modules/.bin/prettier" ]; then
        echo "[format-gate] SKIP (advisory) — systemTest/$p deps not installed (npm ci in systemTest/$p)."
        skipped=$((skipped + 1))
        continue
    fi

    out="$(cd "$dir" && npm run --silent format:check 2>&1)"
    rc=$?
    checked=$((checked + 1))
    if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "[format-gate] systemTest/$p — format:check OK"
        continue
    fi

    failed=$((failed + 1))
    echo "[format-gate] systemTest/$p — format:check FAILED" >&2

    warns="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep '^\[warn\] ' | grep -v 'Code style issues' || true)"

    # A non-zero exit with NO warn lines is not "no problems found" — it is an
    # unexplained failure, and reporting it as clean is the exact shape of a
    # check that cannot fail. Print what actually came back.
    if [ -z "$warns" ]; then
        echo "[format-gate]   prettier exited $rc but named no files. Raw output:" >&2
        printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed 's/^/[format-gate]   | /' >&2
        continue
    fi

    printf '%s\n' "$warns" | while IFS= read -r w; do
        rel="${w#\[warn\] }"
        full="systemTest/$p/$rel"
        # Whose red is this? The whole point of the ticket is that the bill
        # lands on the wrong person. If the file is not in this push, say so —
        # the reader should not have to work that out.
        if [ "$MODE" != "all" ] && printf '%s\n' "$changed_paths" | grep -qx "$full"; then
            echo "[format-gate]   $full   (in this push)" >&2
        elif [ "$MODE" = "all" ]; then
            echo "[format-gate]   $full" >&2
        else
            echo "[format-gate]   $full   (NOT in this push — inherited red)" >&2
        fi
    done

    echo "[format-gate]   fix: (cd systemTest/$p && npm run format)" >&2
# A here-string, NOT a pipe: `... | while read` puts the loop in a SUBSHELL, so
# every counter below would be incremented in a child and read back as 0 here —
# a gate that always reports "0 failed" no matter what prettier said.
done <<< "$selected"

echo "[format-gate] ${checked} package(s) checked, ${skipped} skipped, ${failed} failed"
[ "$failed" -eq 0 ]
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# manifest_path.test.sh — fixtures/manifest.ts names ONE actor manifest per slot (KS-971)
# =============================================================================
# The provisioner writes the generated-actor manifest through fixtures/manifest.ts, whose
# filename rule is fixtures/slot.ts (`manifestFileName`). It used to write ONE shared
# fixtures/generated/actors.json for every slot, so provisioning a second slot overwrote the
# first's actors — found on the four-slot live sweep, 2026-09-07 (KS-682) and independently
# by KS-971. The two fixes met on the develop merge of PR #900 (2026-09-11) and KS-971's rule
# won: the filename carries the slot for EVERY slot, slot 1 included (`actors-slot1.json`,
# never the bare `actors.json`), so provisioning unsourced and reading sourced can never
# look at two different files. KS-682's `fixtures/manifest-path.ts` was removed with it.
#
# fixtures/ has no test runner of its own and the three suites cannot import it (separate
# rootDirs by design), so the rule is pinned here by EXECUTING the module, the way
# slot_target.test.sh pins the shell wrapper. Reached by check-stack-safety.sh's runner loop.
# =============================================================================
set -u
REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
PW="$REPO/systemTest/playwright"
FIX="$REPO/systemTest/fixtures"
PASS=0; FAIL=0
resolve() { # $1 = env assignments as a string; prints the basename, or ERROR:<message>
  ( cd "$PW" && env -u SECUURA_STACK_SLOT -u SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX $1 npx tsx -e \
      "import {manifestPath} from '../fixtures/manifest.ts'; import {basename} from 'node:path'; try { console.log(basename(manifestPath())); } catch (e) { console.log('ERROR:' + e.message); }" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 )
}
case_() { # $1 label, $2 env, $3 expected (exact basename, or a regex prefixed re:)
  local got; got="$(resolve "$2")"
  if [[ "$3" == re:* ]]; then [[ "$got" =~ ${3#re:} ]] && ok="1" || ok=""; else [[ "$got" == "$3" ]] && ok="1" || ok=""; fi
  if [[ -n "$ok" ]]; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); echo "ok   $1"; else FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "FAIL $1 — expected '$3', got '$got'"; fi
}
# Slot 1 is NOT the bare actors.json — that is the KS-971 rule, and a regression to KS-682's
# bare name is asserted as a failure below, not merely as a different green.
case_ "nothing set -> slot 1 -> actors-slot1.json"          ""                                                       "actors-slot1.json"
case_ "slot 1 unsourced -> actors-slot1.json"               "SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=1"                                   "actors-slot1.json"
case_ "slot 1 sourced (-slot1) -> still actors-slot1.json"   "SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=1 SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX=-slot1"   "actors-slot1.json"
case_ "slot 3 unsourced -> actors-slot3.json"               "SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3"                                   "actors-slot3.json"
case_ "slot 3 sourced -> actors-slot3.json (both agree)"    "SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3 SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX=-slot3"   "actors-slot3.json"
case_ "malformed slot is refused, not defaulted to slot 1"   "SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=two"                                 "re:^ERROR:.*must be an integer"
case_ "a slot above the ceiling is refused"                  "SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=44"                                  "re:^ERROR:.*must be in 1\.\.4"
got="$(resolve "")"
if [[ "$got" != "actors.json" ]]; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); echo "ok   the pre-KS-971 bare actors.json is never produced"; else FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "FAIL slot 1 regressed to the bare actors.json"; fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The REJECTED manifest must be scoped exactly like the live one (KS-971 + KS-969)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# It was a module-level const built from a `fixturesDir` that KS-682 had removed,
# so manifest.ts threw `ReferenceError: fixturesDir is not defined` at IMPORT time
# and killed the pre-suite, globalSetup and the whole suite on all four slots
# (merge be47ef22f; found on the live sweep 2026-09-08). Two rules are pinned:
# the module must IMPORT at all, and a degraded run on one slot must not overwrite
# another slot's evidence.
resolve_rejected() { # $1 = env assignments; prints basename, or ERROR:<message>
  ( cd "$PW" && env -u SECUURA_STACK_SLOT -u SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX $1 npx tsx -e \
      "import {rejectedManifestPath} from '../fixtures/manifest.ts'; import {basename} from 'node:path'; try { console.log(basename(rejectedManifestPath())); } catch (e) { console.log('ERROR:' + e.message); }" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 )
}
case_r() { # $1 label, $2 env, $3 expected basename
  local got; got="$(resolve_rejected "$2")"
  if [[ "$got" == "$3" ]]; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); echo "ok   $1"; else FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "FAIL $1 — expected '$3', got '$got'"; fi
}
case_r "rejected: nothing set -> actors.rejected-slot1.json"  ""                        "actors.rejected-slot1.json"
case_r "rejected: slot 1 -> actors.rejected-slot1.json"       "SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=1"    "actors.rejected-slot1.json"
case_r "rejected: slot 3 -> actors.rejected-slot3.json"       "SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3"    "actors.rejected-slot3.json"

# The regression itself: manifest.ts must be IMPORTABLE. The defect was a
# module-level throw, so nothing below the import ever ran — a path assertion
# alone would not have caught it.
import_check() {
  local got
  got="$( cd "$PW" && npx tsx -e \
    "import('../fixtures/manifest.ts').then(() => console.log('IMPORT-OK')).catch((e) => console.log('ERROR:' + e.message));" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 )"
  if [[ "$got" == "IMPORT-OK" ]]; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); echo "ok   manifest.ts imports without throwing"; else FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "FAIL manifest.ts imports without throwing — got '$got'"; fi
}
import_check

# Two slots must not collide on the rejected path either.
a="$(resolve_rejected "SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=2")"; b="$(resolve_rejected "SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=3")"
if [[ "$a" != "$b" ]]; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); echo "ok   rejected manifests differ across slots ($a vs $b)"; else FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "FAIL rejected manifests collide across slots (both '$a')"; fi

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The WRITER must use the resolver, not just agree with it (KS-682)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every case above asks the resolver where a manifest SHOULD go. None of them asks
# writeRejectedManifest where it ACTUALLY put one — so re-hardcoding a fixed path in
# the writer would leave this file entirely green while restoring the shared-file
# defect. KS-971 caps slots at 4, so there is no out-of-range slot to write under;
# slot 4's rejected file is used and whatever was there is put back afterwards.
G="$FIX/generated"; mkdir -p "$G"; KEEP="$(mktemp)"; had=""
[ -f "$G/actors.rejected-slot4.json" ] && { had=1; cp "$G/actors.rejected-slot4.json" "$KEEP"; }
writer_check() {
  local out
  out="$( cd "$PW" && env -u SECUURA_ARTIFACT_SUFFIX SECUURA_STACK_SLOT=4 npx tsx -e \
    "import {writeRejectedManifest} from '../fixtures/manifest.ts';
     import {basename} from 'node:path';
     import {existsSync, rmSync} from 'node:fs';
     try {
       const p = writeRejectedManifest({ baseUrl: 'http://localhost:7182', actors: {} });
       console.log(existsSync(p) ? basename(p) : 'NOT-WRITTEN');
       rmSync(p, { force: true });
     } catch (e) { console.log('ERROR:' + e.message); }" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 )"
  echo "$out"
}
got="$(writer_check)"
[ -n "$had" ] && cp "$KEEP" "$G/actors.rejected-slot4.json"; rm -f "$KEEP"
if [[ "$got" == "actors.rejected-slot4.json" ]]; then
  PASS=$((PASS+1)); echo "ok   writeRejectedManifest writes the SLOT-SCOPED path it returns"
else
  FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "FAIL writeRejectedManifest — expected 'actors.rejected-slot4.json', got '$got'"
fi

echo
echo "manifest_path: ${PASS} passed, ${FAIL} failed"
[[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]]
files.systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh (KS-989)
# =============================================================================
# The gate exists because six formatting reds reached `develop` with nothing
# looking at them. A gate for that class has to be trusted when it says "0
# failed" — so the cases below spend most of their weight on the ways this
# script could report a clean pass while having established nothing:
#
#   * counters incremented inside a SUBSHELL and read back as 0 (a `| while`
#     loop instead of a here-string) — CASE 7;
#   * prettier exiting non-zero while naming no files, reported as clean —
#     CASE 8;
#   * deps missing reported as a FAILURE rather than an environment condition,
#     which is KS-991's whole cost — CASE 6;
#   * a package silently not discovered, so it is never checked — CASE 1.
#
# Every case runs against a FIXTURE repo, not this one: the script derives its
# repo root from its own location, so a copy of it inside a temp tree sees that
# tree's packages and nothing else. The fixture packages' `format:check` scripts
# are plain shell, so no npm install and no real prettier is needed and the
# whole suite runs in seconds.
#
# Usage: bash systemTest/__tests__/package_format_gate.test.sh
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
GATE_SRC="${PACKAGE_FORMAT_GATE_SH:-$HERE/../scripts/check-package-format.sh}"
PASS=0; FAIL=0

[[ -f "$GATE_SRC" ]] || { echo "FATAL: gate script not found at $GATE_SRC" >&2; exit 2; }

FIX="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/secuura-format-gate-test.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$FIX"' EXIT INT TERM

check() {
    local desc="$1" want="$2" got="$3"
    if [[ "$got" == "$want" ]]; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); printf 'ok   %s\n' "$desc"
    else FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); printf 'FAIL %s\n       want "%s", got "%s"\n' "$desc" "$want" "$got"; fi
}

# `expect` is ALSO /usr/bin/expect. A suite that does not define it as a shell
# function does not fail on `expect ...` — it shells out to the binary, which
# exits 0 having compared nothing, and every case still prints ok. That happened
# for real in stack_guard.test.sh (KS-691).
expect() { check "$@"; }
if [[ "$(type -t expect)" != "function" ]]; then
    printf 'FATAL: expect is not a shell function (resolves to %s) — cases would pass vacuously.\n' \
        "$(command -v expect)" >&2
    exit 2
fi

# --- fixture builders ---------------------------------------------------------
GATE="$FIX/systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh"
mkdir -p "$FIX/systemTest/scripts"
cp "$GATE_SRC" "$GATE"

# mk_pkg <name> <format:check shell command> <with_deps: yes|no>
mk_pkg() {
    local name="$1" cmd="$2" deps="$3"
    local dir="$FIX/systemTest/$name"
    mkdir -p "$dir"
    cat > "$dir/package.json" <<JSON
{ "name": "fixture-$name", "version": "0.0.0", "scripts": { "format:check": "$cmd" } }
JSON
    if [[ "$deps" == "yes" ]]; then
        mkdir -p "$dir/node_modules/.bin"
        printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > "$dir/node_modules/.bin/prettier"
        chmod +x "$dir/node_modules/.bin/prettier"
    fi
}

# a package with NO format:check script at all — must never be discovered
mk_pkg_no_script() {
    local dir="$FIX/systemTest/$1"
    mkdir -p "$dir"
    printf '{ "name": "fixture-%s", "version": "0.0.0", "scripts": { "test": "true" } }\n' "$1" > "$dir/package.json"
}

mk_pkg green    "exit 0"                                         yes
mk_pkg red      "echo '[warn] src/a.ts'; exit 1"                 yes
mk_pkg red2     "echo '[warn] src/b.ts'; exit 1"                 yes
mk_pkg silent   "exit 3"                                         yes    # non-zero, names nothing
mk_pkg nodeps   "exit 0"                                         no     # deps absent
mk_pkg_no_script plain

run_gate() { printf '%s\n' "$1" | bash "$GATE" 2>&1; }

# --- CASE 1: packages are DISCOVERED, not listed ------------------------------
# A hardcoded list is a second implementation of reality that nothing keeps in
# agreement. The gate must find a package by its format:check script alone.
listing="$(bash "$GATE" --list 2>&1)"
check "discovers a package that declares format:check" "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$listing" | grep -cx 'green')"
check "discovers every such package (5 fixtures)"      "5" "$(printf '%s\n' "$listing" | grep -cE '^(green|red|red2|silent|nodeps)$')"
# ...and the negative half: a package WITHOUT the script is not in scope. Without
# this, "discovery works" would be satisfied by a gate that returns everything.
check "does NOT discover a package with no format:check" "0" "$(printf '%s\n' "$listing" | grep -cx 'plain')"

# --- CASE 2: only the touched package is checked ------------------------------
out="$(run_gate 'systemTest/green/docs/x.md')"
check "a path in green selects green"      "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'systemTest/green — format:check OK')"
check "...and does not run red"            "0" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'systemTest/red ')"
check "one package checked, none failed"   "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '1 package(s) checked, 0 skipped, 0 failed')"

# --- CASE 3: a push touching no gated package costs nothing -------------------
# The hook's header promises it "stays out of the way". If this case ever prints
# or exits non-zero, every Blockchain/Dev push pays for a gate that found nothing.
out="$(run_gate 'Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/index.ts')"; rc=$?
check "no gated path -> exit 0"       "0" "$rc"
check "no gated path -> says nothing" ""  "$out"
# A path under systemTest/ but not inside a package must behave the same way.
out="$(run_gate 'systemTest/docs/readme.md')"
check "systemTest path outside any package -> silent" "" "$out"

# --- CASE 4: a red package fails, and names the file --------------------------
out="$(run_gate 'systemTest/red/src/a.ts')"; rc=$?
check "a red package -> exit 1"            "1" "$rc"
check "...names the offending file"        "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'systemTest/red/src/a.ts')"
check "...and says how to fix it"          "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'cd systemTest/red && npm run format')"

# --- CASE 5: whose red is it? -------------------------------------------------
# The ticket's actual complaint is that the bill lands on the wrong person. The
# gate must say whether the red file is in YOUR push or inherited.
out="$(run_gate 'systemTest/red/src/a.ts')"
check "a red file IN the push is labelled so"      "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'src/a.ts   (in this push)')"
out="$(run_gate 'systemTest/red/docs/unrelated.md')"
check "a red file NOT in the push is labelled so"  "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'src/a.ts   (NOT in this push — inherited red)')"

# --- CASE 6: deps missing is an ENVIRONMENT condition, not a failure ----------
# KS-991: an environment condition presented as a gate failure cost a diagnosis
# five times in one day. It must skip, loudly, naming the remedy — and exit 0.
out="$(run_gate 'systemTest/nodeps/src/a.ts')"; rc=$?
check "deps missing -> exit 0"                "0" "$rc"
check "deps missing -> SKIP (advisory)"       "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'SKIP (advisory) — systemTest/nodeps deps not installed')"
check "deps missing -> names the remedy"      "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'npm ci in systemTest/nodeps')"
check "deps missing -> counted as skipped"    "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '0 package(s) checked, 1 skipped, 0 failed')"

# --- CASE 7: THE COUNTER MUST SURVIVE THE LOOP --------------------------------
# `... | while read` puts the loop in a subshell: every counter is incremented in
# a child and read back as 0 here, so the trailer reads "0 failed" no matter what
# prettier said — a gate that cannot fail. Two red packages in one run is what
# discriminates; one red would pass even with a broken counter if the exit code
# happened to be right.
out="$(printf '%s\n' 'systemTest/red/src/a.ts
systemTest/red2/src/b.ts' | bash "$GATE" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
check "two red packages -> exit 1"                    "1" "$rc"
check "two red packages -> trailer counts BOTH"       "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '2 package(s) checked, 0 skipped, 2 failed')"
# ...and the positive control for the same trailer: a mixed run counts correctly
# too, so the "2 failed" above is not a constant.
out="$(printf '%s\n' 'systemTest/red/src/a.ts
systemTest/green/src/c.ts' | bash "$GATE" 2>&1)"
check "mixed run -> trailer counts one failure"       "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '2 package(s) checked, 0 skipped, 1 failed')"

# --- CASE 8: a non-zero exit that names NO files is not a pass ----------------
# "Empty output is never a zero." A checker that fails without naming a file has
# established nothing; reporting that as clean is the exact shape of the reds
# this gate exists to catch.
out="$(run_gate 'systemTest/silent/src/a.ts')"; rc=$?
check "non-zero with no [warn] lines -> exit 1"      "1" "$rc"
check "...counted as a failure, not a pass"          "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '1 package(s) checked, 0 skipped, 1 failed')"
check "...says prettier named no files"              "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'exited 3 but named no files')"

# --- CASE 9: --all ignores stdin and checks everything ------------------------
# This is the KS-854/KS-882 arm: when no informative base can be computed, an
# empty changed set must not be read as a clean tree.
out="$(bash "$GATE" --all 2>&1)"; rc=$?
check "--all -> exit 1 (fixtures include reds)"  "1" "$rc"
check "--all checks the untouched green package" "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c 'systemTest/green — format:check OK')"
check "--all checks every deps-present package"  "1" "$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c '4 package(s) checked, 1 skipped, 3 failed')"

# --- CASE 10: usage errors are refused, not guessed at ------------------------
bash "$GATE" --nonsense >/dev/null 2>&1
check "an unknown flag -> exit 2" "2" "$?"

echo ""
echo "package_format_gate: ${PASS} passed, ${FAIL} failed"
(( FAIL == 0 ))
